summary: Comprehensive first-run testing of AddisFix (civic reporting). Wrote /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (42 pytest cases) covering auth, authorization matrix, uploads, real AI analyze, report creation + incident engine linking/deduplication, public incidents, confirm/follow idempotency, authority lifecycle + invalid transitions, follower notifications, admin stats/users/roles/status/audit, and categories/departments CRUD. All 42 pass serially (-n 0). Frontend e2e via Playwright: landing loads, citizen registration sets cookies and redirects to dashboard, /map shows Leaflet markers from real seeded + user data, /report 4-step stepper works end-to-end (upload JPEG -> AI card renders -> picker-map click sets coords -> fill details -> submit), lands on /incidents/{id}, confirm-btn and follow-btn update counts, admin dashboard and authority dashboard both load real stats (36 users, 34 reports, 12 incidents) without errors.

issues: Representative image container is very large (fixed height) and when the image is a small/plain upload it stretches awkwardly - consider object-fit:cover and max-height

action_items: None - all backend endpoints and critical UI flows work. Keep pytest.ini addopts; agents must run with `-n 0` for sequential or ensure fixtures are not shared across xdist workers (module-scoped fixtures do not cross workers under --dist loadscope).
Optional UX: tighten representative image sizing on incident detail (currently stretches)
critical_code_review_comments: process_report() excludes only resolved/rejected incidents when searching for matches - a new report near an incident that is already assigned/in_progress will still link to it (by design). Looks correct but worth documenting.

ReportPage.jsx sets explicit `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` on the axios upload call (line 66). This usually works because axios overrides it with the proper boundary, but relying on this is fragile; prefer letting axios set the header automatically.

/api/incidents/{id}/follow is non-idempotent on the backend (increments follower_count only when no existing follow) but the frontend GET returns `following: true` either way - good. DELETE follow does `$inc: -1` with no floor; if called twice (not possible via UI) counter could go negative - consider using update_one with existence check or atomic conditional.
test_credentials: Used admin dagmawiaddisu94@gmail.com/AddisFix@2026, authority demo.authority@addisfix.demo/Demo@2026, and dynamically registered citizens. Credentials file /app/memory/test_credentials.md present and correct.
seed_data_creation: No seeding needed - app seeds demo data on startup. Tests do create ephemeral users (register fresh), reports and incidents at Bole (9.0106,38.7613) and at random far southern-hemisphere coordinates to avoid cross-run collisions.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file is at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py. pytest.ini defaults to `-n 2 --dist loadscope` which splits classes across workers; because the `citizen` fixture is module-scoped and some tests mutate the dict (first_incident_id, file_id), running with xdist causes KeyErrors. Always run with `-n 0` or restructure fixture to be test-local. Preview URL: https://addisfix-demo.preview.emergentagent.com. AI is real (gpt-4o-mini) and returns available=true with category/severity/description/confidence/model fields on real images. Reports are persistent in Mongo (test_database) across runs, so any 'far point creates new incident' assertion must use a fresh random coordinate.
rca of the issue: No product bugs identified. Two transient test failures during tuning were test-data-persistence related: (1) 'far report creates new incident' used a fixed coordinate (9.05, 38.80) that collided with previously-created test incidents; fixed by using a random far coordinate. (2) xdist parallelism broke module-scoped mutable fixture sharing; mitigated by running `-n 0`.
